question: What typical Chevron Alignment sign spacing does Table 2C-5 recommend for an advisory speed of 35 to 45 mph and a curve radius of 401 to 700 feet?
model_answer: Direct Answer: For an advisory speed of 35 to 45 mph and a curve radius of 401 to 700 feet, Table 2C-5 shows a typical Chevron Alignment sign spacing of 120 feet. This spacing is a Guidance value, measured along the turn or curve from the point of curvature (PC). Standards (mandatory): - "If used, Chevron Alignment signs shall be installed on the outside of a turn or curve, in line with and at approximately a right angle to approaching traffic. Chevron Alignment signs shall be installed at a minimum height of 4 feet, measured vertically from the bottom of the sign to the elevation of the near edge of the traveled way." Guidance (recommended): - "The approximate spacing of Chevron Alignment signs on the turn or curve measured from the point of curvature (PC) should be as shown in Table 2C-5." - Per Table 2C-5, for an advisory speed of 35 to 45 mph with a curve radius of 401 to 700 feet, the sign spacing is 120 feet. Visual evidence: - [Image 1] Table 2C-5 shows the row "35 to 45 mph / 401 to 700 feet / 120 feet," along with a note that the relationship between curve radius and advisory speed in the table should not be used to determine the advisory speed. - [Image 2] Figure 2C-2 (Sheet 1 of 2, A – Curve) illustrates W1-8 Chevron Alignment signs placed along the outside of a curve, with a note directing users to Table 2C-5 for spacing of W1-8 signs. Citations: - Section 2C.08 Guidance §5 (p.158) - Section 2C.08 Standard §4 (p.158) - Table 2C-5 (p.158) - Figure 2C-2 (p.156)
